headline: Ward 6 lands 44th of 50, with the city's highest reported violent crime rate.
summary:
Ward 6 covers Greater Grand Crossing, Chatham, Englewood, and Roseland on Chicago's South Side. Of the fifty wards, it lands 44th. That rank comes from a composite score of 32.14, in the lower half of the citywide range.

The ward's clearest strengths are in retail character and city administration. Just 1.54 percent of its licensed food stores belong to one of the 100 largest retail chains, the lowest share in Chicago, and its building permits move through the city faster than in nearly every other ward. Safety and demographics pull the other way. Ward 6 carries the highest reported violent crime rate of the 50 wards, the lowest share of multilingual households, and one of the thinnest counts of sit-down restaurants per resident. Most of its food retail stays independent of the big chains, even as crime and language diversity remain real weak points.
reading_the_rankings: Start with the worst number. Ward 6's violent crime rate runs about 709 incidents per 10,000 residents, the highest reading among the 50 wards. The count starts with census tracts, each one split evenly across its area regardless of where people actually cluster inside it, and then laid onto the ward map, so a tract only partly inside Ward 6 still contributes its full share here. Confidence in the number is only medium, by the compiler's own admission. Two of Ward 6's best numbers deserve a similar gut check. Its first-place ranks on modeled religious attendance and modeled daily leisure time are not measurements taken inside the ward at all. They're a profile, built from national survey data, describing what places sharing this area's demographic mix tend to look like elsewhere, not a local count of anyone's actual habits here. The people behind the model rate it low confidence, for both figures alike. Ward 6's first-place rank on the parks share of aldermanic menu money is a real number, but it comes with its own asterisk. Boundaries moved in 2023, and part of what's being counted here may still carry the ward's old shape rather than its current one. On top of that, some wards are simply missing from this one entirely, so the citywide comparison isn't running on the same footing for everyone.

news.headline: Mini Soccer Field, Pickleball Court, Media Lab Coming To These South Side Parks
news.note: Coverage of aldermanic menu fund improvements underway at Tuley Park and Cole Park in Chatham, including a new miniature soccer field and pickleball court.

news.headline: Can Indie Pharmacies Serve Areas Abandoned By Walgreens? New Plan Aims To Do Just That
news.note: Reporting on a proposed city Office of Pharmacy Access and a pop-up pharmacy storefront planned for 79th Street after a Walgreens closure in the ward.
